title: Economic Nowcasting with Bridge Equations and Real-Time Evaluation
text: GDP published lag, typically 6 8 weeks quarter ends. monthly indicators like retail sales, industrial production, labour market data arrive much sooner. Nowcasting uses higher-frequency series estimate GDP growth real time, official number appears. core challenge ragged edge: different indicators different publication lags. Retail sales might available February, industrial production January, employment December, calendar date. nowcasting model must handle jagged pattern data availability. nowcast aligns mixed-frequency data, estimates bridge equations (standard model central banks), evaluates nowcast performance pseudo-real-time backtesting.

what: How does nowcast compare to other packages?
title: Economic Nowcasting with Bridge Equations and Real-Time Evaluation
text: nowcast provides bridge equations integrated evaluation lightweight package. bridgr bridge equations within tidyverse ecosystem. midasr mature MIDAS implementation. dfms high-quality DFM package C++ backend. nowcast focuses evaluation side: pseudo-real-time backtesting HLN-corrected Diebold-Mariano test let compare nowcasting specifications data.

title: Economic Nowcasting with Bridge Equations and Real-Time Evaluation
code: library(nowcast)  # Quarterly target (e.g. GDP growth) gdp <- data.frame(   date = seq(as.Date("2015-01-01"), by = "quarter", length.out = 40),   value = rnorm(40, 0.5, 0.3) )  # Monthly indicators (e.g. retail sales, industrial production) retail <- data.frame(   date = seq(as.Date("2015-01-01"), by = "month", length.out = 120),   value = rnorm(120, 0.4, 0.5) ) ip <- data.frame(   date = seq(as.Date("2015-01-01"), by = "month", length.out = 118),  # ragged edge   value = rnorm(118, 0.3, 0.4) )  # Align: monthly indicators are averaged to quarterly frequency aligned <- nc_align(gdp, retail = retail, ip = ip) aligned #> ── Aligned Nowcasting Dataset ── #> • Target: target (quarterly) #> • Indicators: 2 (retail, ip) #> • Periods: 40 (2015-01-01 to 2024-10-01)  # See the ragged edge nc_ragged_edge(aligned)

title: Economic Nowcasting with Bridge Equations and Real-Time Evaluation
code: # Bridge equation with AR(1) term (default) result <- nc_bridge(target ~ retail + ip, data = aligned) result #> ── Nowcast (Bridge Equation) ── #> • Nowcast: 0.4832 #> • SE: 0.3156 #> • 95% CI: [-0.1467, 1.1131] #> • Target period: 2024-10-01 #> • R-squared: 0.1523 | Obs: 38  # Full summary with coefficients summary(result)  # Static bridge equation (no AR terms) nc_bridge(target ~ retail + ip, data = aligned, ar_order = 0)

title: Economic Nowcasting with Bridge Equations and Real-Time Evaluation
code: # Expanding-window backtest: train on 1:i-1, nowcast i bt <- nc_backtest(target ~ retail + ip, data = aligned, start = 20) bt #> ── Nowcast Backtest (bridge, expanding) ── #> • Evaluations: 18 #> • RMSE: 0.2847 #> • MAE: 0.2312 #> • Bias: 0.0043  # Compare two specifications bt_static <- nc_backtest(target ~ retail + ip, data = aligned,                           start = 20, ar_order = 0) nc_dm_test(bt$results$error, bt_static$results$error) #> Diebold-Mariano (HLN): p = 0.42  # Plot actual vs nowcast plot(bt)

title: Economic Nowcasting with Bridge Equations and Real-Time Evaluation
text: Bridge equations widely used nowcasting method. developed ECB (Runstler Sedillot 2003, Baffigi et al. 2004) remain standard model central banks treasuries. idea simple: aggregate monthly indicators quarterly frequency, regress quarterly target aggregated indicators. Following standard practice, nc_bridge() includes autoregressive term default (ar_order = 1) capture GDP momentum. model : yt=α+ϕyt−1+∑iβix‾,t+εty_t = \alpha + \phi y_{t-1} + \sum_i \beta_i \bar{x}_{,t} + \varepsilon_t x‾,t\bar{x}_{,t} within-quarter mean monthly indicator ii. Prediction intervals come predict.lm(..., interval = "prediction"), accounts residual variance coefficient estimation uncertainty, evaluated t distribution.

title: Economic Nowcasting with Bridge Equations and Real-Time Evaluation
text: nc_dm_test() function implements Harvey, Leybourne, Newbold (1997) modification Diebold-Mariano (1995) test. HLN correction applies finite-sample scaling factor uses t_{n-1} distribution rather standard normal. matters sample sizes typical nowcasting (20-60 quarters). Bartlett (triangular) kernel used HAC variance estimation, guarantees non-negative variance.

title: Economic Nowcasting with Bridge Equations and Real-Time Evaluation
text: nc_backtest() performs pseudo-real-time evaluation final revised data. step, model sees past data (expanding rolling window) produces nowcast next period. simulates real-time performance account data revisions. True real-time evaluation requires vintage data (e.g. FRED’s ALFRED database).

title: Economic Nowcasting with Bridge Equations and Real-Time Evaluation
text: nc_ prefix. Short, distinctive, easy type autocomplete. AR terms default. GDP growth serially correlated. Following ECB/BoE practice, nc_bridge() includes AR(1) term default. Set ar_order = 0 static specification. Prediction intervals. Uses full prediction standard error (estimation uncertainty + residual variance) t quantiles, just residual standard deviation normal quantiles. HLN-corrected DM test. original Diebold-Mariano test -rejects small samples. HLN correction now standard (used forecast::dm.test R statsmodels Python). heavy dependencies. Depends cli stats. tidyverse, Rcpp, external system libraries. Pure computation. download data. Pair ons, boe, fred, data source.

title: Economic Nowcasting with Bridge Equations and Real-Time Evaluation
text: Bridge equations . MIDAS regressions dynamic factor models implemented. MIDAS, see midasr. DFMs, see dfms. Pseudo-real-time evaluation . backtest uses final revised data, vintage data. Data revisions can material (Banbura et al. 2013, ECB WP 1564). True real-time evaluation requires vintage data user must supply. automatic indicator forecasting ragged edge. 1-2 months current quarter available, nc_bridge() uses whatever user provides newdata. forecast missing months AR/ARIMA. Central bank implementations typically , adds model-within-model complexity. OLS standard errors. reported coefficient standard errors assume homoskedastic, serially uncorrelated errors. Durbin-Watson statistic reported result$details$dw_stat help diagnose autocorrelation. HAC-robust inference, extract fitted model via result$model use sandwich package.

title: Pseudo-Real-Time Backtesting — nc_backtest
text: pseudo-real-time exercise: uses final revised data throughout, data available point time (vintage data). noted Banbura et al. (2013, ECB WP 1564), data revisions can material variables, results may overstate true real-time accuracy. Prediction intervals computed using full prediction standard error predict.lm(..., interval = "prediction"), accounting residual variance coefficient estimation uncertainty.

title: Pseudo-Real-Time Backtesting — nc_backtest
code: # \donttest{ set.seed(42) n <- 30 d <- data.frame(   date = seq(as.Date("2015-01-01"), by = "quarter", length.out = n),   gdp = cumsum(rnorm(n, 0.5, 0.3)),   ind1 = cumsum(rnorm(n, 0.4, 0.2)) ) bt <- nc_backtest(gdp ~ ind1, data = d, start = 15) bt #>  #> ── Nowcast Backtest (bridge, expanding) ──────────────────────────────────────── #> • Evaluations: 15 #> • Period: 2018-10-01 to 2022-04-01 #> • RMSE: 0.526 #> • MAE: 0.3943 #> • Bias: -0.0845 # }

title: Bridge Equation Nowcast — nc_bridge
text: Estimate bridge equation via OLS produce nowcast current specified period. Bridge equations translate higher-frequency indicators (e.g. monthly) estimates lower-frequency target (e.g. quarterly GDP). Following standard central bank practice (Baffigi et al. 2004, Runstler Sedillot 2003), autoregressive term target variable can included via ar_order argument.

NULL, last complete row data used. ar_order Integer. Number autoregressive lags target include (default 1). Set 0 static bridge equation AR terms. alpha Numeric. Significance level prediction intervals (default 0.05).

title: Bridge Equation Nowcast — nc_bridge
text: Prediction intervals computed using full prediction standard error, accounts residual variance estimation uncertainty coefficients, evaluated t distribution appropriate degrees freedom. ar_order > 0, model includes lagged dependent variable. reported standard errors assume homoskedastic, serially uncorrelated errors. residuals exhibit autocorrelation (indicated Durbin-Watson statistic details$dw_stat), consider extracting fitted model via result$model applying HAC standard errors sandwich package.

what: Diebold-Mariano Test for Equal Predictive Accuracy — nc_dm_test
title: Diebold-Mariano Test for Equal Predictive Accuracy — nc_dm_test
text: Tests whether two sets forecast errors equal predictive accuracy. Implements modified test Harvey, Leybourne, Newbold (1997), applies finite-sample correction original Diebold Mariano (1995) statistic uses t distribution rather normal. Bartlett (triangular) kernel used HAC variance estimation, guarantees non-negative variance estimate.

"two.sided", "less" (model 1 better), "greater" (model 2 better). h Integer. Forecast horizon (default 1). Used Newey-West bandwidth HLN correction. loss Character. Loss function: "squared" "absolute".

what: nowcast: Economic Nowcasting with Bridge Equations and Real-Time Evaluation — nowcast-package
title: nowcast: Economic Nowcasting with Bridge Equations and Real-Time Evaluation — nowcast-package
text: Provides bridge equations optional autoregressive terms nowcasting low-frequency macroeconomic variables (e.g. quarterly GDP) higher-frequency indicators (e.g. monthly retail sales). Handles ragged-edge problem different indicators different publication lags via mixed-frequency alignment. Includes pseudo-real-time evaluation expanding rolling windows, Diebold-Mariano test comparing forecast accuracy following Harvey, Leybourne, Newbold (1997) doi:10.1016/S0169-2070(96)00719-4 . API calls; designed work data source.
